# Five seeds per configuration: columns come from the one key that
# differs, seed is the replicate, and each Final row is a paired t test
# on per-seed differences.

exec trainstat -skip 1 $TESTDATA/sweep/base.txt $TESTDATA/sweep/new.txt
cmp stdout want

# Paired: n=5 gives 4 degrees of freedom; the interval matches
# mean(d) ± t(0.975,4)·sd(d)/√5 = 0.0056 ± 2.776·0.00114/2.236.
stdout 'Final/split=val .* \+0\.0056  \[\+0\.0042, \+0\.0070\]  p<0\.001 n=5 paired'

# CSV has the same cells without separators.
exec trainstat -skip 1 -format csv $TESTDATA/sweep/base.txt $TESTDATA/sweep/new.txt
stdout '^accuracy,5e-4,1e-3,,,,$'
stdout '^Final/split=val,0\.8022 ± 0\.0024,0\.8078 ± 0\.0038,\+0\.0056,"\[\+0\.0042, \+0\.0070\]",p<0\.001 n=5 paired,$'

# Seeds whose validation sets differ are not paired: Welch, with a note.
exec trainstat v1.txt v2.txt
stdout '^Final +0\.510 ± 0\.025 +0\.613 ± 0\.038  \+0\.103  \[\+0\.072, \+0\.135\]  p=0\.001 n=3 welch \(unpaired: validation sets differ for replicate 2\)$'

# A relative unit with several rows gets a geometric mean row, unless a
# value is not positive.
exec trainstat g1.txt g2.txt
stdout '^geomean +4\.000 +2\.000 +-50\.00%$'
stdout -count=1 geomean

# An explicit column overrides the automatic choice.
exec trainstat -skip 1 -col .file $TESTDATA/sweep/base.txt $TESTDATA/sweep/new.txt
stdout '^columns: \.file$'

-- v1.txt --
seed: 1
val_sha256: a
BenchmarkFinal 1 0.5 accuracy
seed: 2
val_sha256: b
BenchmarkFinal 1 0.52 accuracy
seed: 3
val_sha256: c
BenchmarkFinal 1 0.51 accuracy
-- v2.txt --

BenchmarkFinal 1 0.6 accuracy
seed: 2

BenchmarkFinal 1 0.63 accuracy
seed: 3
val_sha256: c
BenchmarkFinal 1 0.61 accuracy
